summary: The equal-tail lemma and the subsequent box-section optimization support the boxed numerical estimate if one grants a sufficiently strong, precise transverse-limit hypothesis. The candidate nevertheless does not prove its full stated conclusion, and the transverse convergence assumption is not specified well enough for a stateless audit of the limiting steps.
critical_errors: The final "In particular" assertion does not follow from (7) under the supplied hypotheses. The quantities P_{\varnothing,n} and K_n are never defined, and no hypothesis identifies P_{\varnothing,n} with P_n or gives |K_n|/|K| -> 1. Thus the displayed escape balance can hold for objects unrelated to P_n and K without contradicting (7).
gaps: The phrase "standard transverse needle limit" is not a mathematical definition. The proof needs, but the statement does not explicitly guarantee, a common anisotropic normalization under which the normalized section-length functions of E_n intersect Q_{3,n} converge with their integrals, the two nonparallel boundaries converge to the longitudinal cuts t=l and t=1-s, and the support minima used in (26) converge. Merely saying that boundaries and exact cells converge does not specify a topology or these consequences.

The passage from the limiting inequalities (24)-(26) to the limsup area bound is only asserted. A complete proof should define the exact finite-n upper widths 2+h_{i,n}+min_{E_n} ell_i, show their convergence together with H_n=sum_i h_{i,n}, and invoke continuity or upper semicontinuity of the clipped-simplex area. It should also separately dispose of a nonpositive limiting width before using the equal-width maximization.
repair_hints: Define P_{\varnothing,n} and K_n and add the exact identifications or convergence relations that turn (7) into a contradiction with the escape balance, or delete the unsupported "In particular" conclusion.
Replace the informal transverse-limit phrase by explicit normalized-set or section-function convergence assumptions sufficient to justify (19)-(26).
Insert the finite-n coordinate containment and the short continuity argument that converts it into the claimed limsup bound.
